executive-summary.verdict: REGRESSION CONFIRMED - Overhead accumulation exceeds component gains

test-corpus.description: Synthetic JSON documents (realistic LLM training data)

analysis.root-cause: Component-level speedups insufficient to overcome integration overhead

evidence.point: Baseline and optimized overlapping confidence intervals (minimal separation)
High outlier percentage (10-16%) suggests high variability in Phase 3.8 code
Regression trend consistent across warmup and measurement phases
Formula-based claims (3×) do not account for integration overhead

bottleneck.title: Buffer Allocation Overhead

root-cause.description: Vec allocations in batch_streaming_loader.rs + StreamingBuffer buffer copying

evidence.item: Every document triggers Vec::extend_from_slice() in streaming buffer
Buffer pool reuse (line 91: Vec::with_capacity(BUFFER_SIZE)) doesn't prevent allocations
Batch-to-main buffer copy on flush (lines 187-189)
Zero-copy optimization NOT implemented - still using String/Vec conversions

expected-impact.cumulative: Adds up across 10K documents: 13K-26K ns total

bottleneck.fix-tier: T5 Streaming (zero-copy iterator instead of Vec copies)

fix-strategy.option: Replace Vec buffer with ring buffer iterator (zero allocations)
Use Arc<str> for lazy materialization (defer copy to consumer)
Implement batch processing with references instead of owned Vecs

bottleneck.title: Atomic CAS Contention

root-cause.description: DualAtomicU64 generation counter CAS operations on LSH batch inserts

evidence.item: BatchLshIndex maintains generation counter for consistency checks
Each batch insert triggers CAS on generation (CompareExchange or SeqCst)
Not using Relaxed ordering - unnecessarily strong memory barriers
Per-band bucket updates (5 bands × batch_size CAS operations)

expected-impact.per-batch: 1000 batch × 5 bands = 5000 CAS operations per batch
expected-impact.cumulative: For 10K docs: 150-400 ns total (0.01-0.03% of 13µs baseline)

bottleneck.fix-tier: T1 Atomic (Relaxed memory ordering for reads)

fix-strategy.option: Use Acquire/Release only at batch boundaries (not per-insert)
Switch to Relaxed ordering for generation counter reads (no sync needed)
Batch multiple inserts before checking generation

root-cause.description: Arc<str> allocations during JSON field extraction (lines 107-111)

evidence.item: Each JSON field extracted as Arc<str> (atomic reference counted string)
Arc::from() involves atomic allocation + reference count initialization
SIMD window search (lines 107-111) followed by Arc wrapping (implicit)
Per-field overhead accumulates across multiple fields per document

expected-impact.fields-per-doc: 3-5 fields per JSON document (id, text, metadata)
expected-impact.cumulative: 10K docs × 250 ns = 2.5 µs total (0.02% of 13µs baseline)

fix-strategy.option: Preallocate Arc pool (128-512 Arc<str> instances, reuse across batches)
Defer Arc wrapping until consumer needs (lazy initialization)

bottleneck.title: HashMap Contention (Batch LSH Merge)

root-cause.description: HashMap merge for batch bucket accumulation (lines 187-189)

evidence.item: Each batch creates local HashMap (line 165)
On flush, merges into global HashMap via append() (lines 187-189)
HashMap::entry() calls hash function + lookup on merge (O(1) amortized)
Not optimal for batched inserts - vector append would be faster

bottleneck.fix-tier: T4 Batch (vector sort + merge for sorted buckets)

fix-strategy.option: Use Vec<(key, vec)> sorted by key (faster merge via linear scan)
Pre-allocate buckets HashMap with capacity (avoid rehashing)
Use BTreeMap for stable iteration order + merge performance

explained-overhead.conclusion: Overhead fully explains measured regression (within range)

unexamined-overhead.hypothesis: Some overhead sources cannot be profiled (perf restricted)

compound-independent.title: If Truly Independent (FALSE)
compound-independent.assumption: Both optimizations apply to non-overlapping phases
compound-independent.reality: FALSE - SIMD JSON is just part of loading, Batch LSH causes overhead elsewhere

explanation.item: Net result: Speedups completely negated by overhead

conclusion.statement: Claimed 3× speedup VIOLATES Amdahl's Law for this workload
conclusion.delta: Measured 1.27× worse than even optimistic Amdahl projection

hypothesis-1.title: Component Optimizations Too Weak

evidence.item: SIMD JSON speedup (2×) applies only to loading phase (40% of pipeline)
Batch LSH speedup (1.5×) applies to 20% of pipeline
Theoretical maximum from components: 1.27× (Amdahl limit)
Overhead alone (2%) explains entire regression

hypothesis-1.conclusion: Component benefits completely negated by integration overhead

hypothesis-2.title: Buffer Operations Dominate New Overhead

evidence.item: StreamingBufferCapsule uses Vec::extend_from_slice per document
Batch buffer allocation/deallocation cycles
Buffer pool not reusing allocations (lines 91, 116)
1-2% overhead aligns with buffer copy cost estimate

hypothesis-2.conclusion: Primary overhead source: buffer allocation and copying

hypothesis-3.title: Atomic Operations Not Optimized for Batch Context

evidence.item: DualAtomicU64 generation counter uses SeqCst/Acquire instead of Relaxed
5000+ CAS operations per batch (5 bands × 1000 docs)
Memory barriers on each CAS add up to 0.01-0.03% overhead
Not a major factor (explains ~0.02% of 2% regression)

hypothesis-3.conclusion: Minor contributor to overhead, not primary factor
hypothesis-3.confidence: MEDIUM - Estimated from atomic operation latencies

secondary-bottleneck.name: Arc Allocations in JSON Parser (0.02% overhead)

fix.current-tier: T5 Streaming (but implemented incorrectly - uses Vec copies)

approach.description: Implement true zero-copy streaming using iterator protocol

steps.step: Replace Vec buffer with ring buffer iterator
Use Arc<str> for lazy materialization (defer copy)
Implement batch_iter() that yields &str references (no allocation)

approach.description: Pre-allocate Arc pool for JSON fields

steps.step: Reuse Arc instances across batch operations

approach.description: Switch to Relaxed ordering where sync not needed

steps.step: Use load(Relaxed) for generation counter reads (most operations)
Keep SeqCst only at batch boundaries (required for consistency)
